title: York man was held at gunpoint over incorrect Flock hit. Sheriff blames illegal tag cover

reading.body:
This is a false positive from an automated identification system that was acted on as if it were confirmed. A license-plate reader misread the first letter of a plate and matched a BMW to a similar stolen vehicle. The match was treated as grounds for a stop, and the man it pointed to was held at gunpoint for more than five minutes.

The failure sits at the handoff from machine output to police action, not in the reading alone. The vendor's own position is that alerts of this kind require independent checks before officers act, and that check is what would have caught the error before anyone was detained. The sheriff's office attributes the misread to an illegal tinted plate cover, which, if it were the cause, would put the reading outside the conditions the system was built to handle.

What is not established is that the plate cover caused the misread, because that is the department's account rather than an independent finding. The department's description of the deputy's actions as reasonable is likewise its own judgement, not a ruling by anyone else.

reports.title: York man was held at gunpoint over incorrect Flock hit. Sheriff blames illegal tag cover

summary: Steven Melvin, 42, of York County, South Carolina, was held at gunpoint for more than five minutes after a Flock Safety license-plate reader misread the first letter of his plate and matched his BMW to a similar stolen vehicle. The sheriff’s office later said an illegal tinted plate cover caused the error and called the deputy’s actions reasonable. Flock said such alerts need independent checks before police action.
